dialogs.text:
Hello my good Traveller!
Welcome to the world of Galdaria.
Your first task is to purge these lands of every creature in these woods!
I am a bit too old to run around and kill, but I have scouted out the area for you.
Currently, these pesky creatures are running around. Happy little bastards...
Kill them for me, and I will grant you access to my torture chamber!
When the deed is done, you will find a portal in a cave to the north.
Are you up for the task?

Excellent choice!
I promise you won't regret it!
Talk to you later.

Uhm ok...
Listen. Here is the issue.
You can dwell on this as long as you want.
But as long as these creatures are still alive you will not be able to progress.
Up to you hippie! Peace & Love!
So will you help me?

Maybe!!??
How am I supposed to respond to that??
At least have the decency to make up a choice!
I presume you are capable of that! So spit it out.
Yes or No?

Wow...
Well done you fucking psycho-killer.
Did it ever occur to you that some of them have a family??
Oh well, you can now proceed further through the portal into the next level

Oh hello again!
These moss-covered zombies attacked me, and I lost all my money when I ran.
Since you are already running around on your killing spree,
Can you collect the coins and return to me?

Hey!
That money belongs to me!
Didn't your mother teach you stealing is wrong!?
So I'm asking again; Can you collect the coins and return to me?

Whoah there!
No need to get all pumped up!
Watch so you don't pop a blood vessel or something.
So I'm asking again; Can you collect the coins and return to me?

Watch your tongue traveller!
I do not respond well to insults
So I'm asking again; Can you collect the coins and return to me?

Ah well.
A maybe is better than nothing.
Especially coming from such a lowlife like yourself.
Come see me when you have collected at least 10 gold for me.

How about this..
You worry about your problems and I deal with mine.
OK?
Geez. What's with all the questions detective?
Piss off!

What do you need? I'm in the middle of something.
Those creatures outside are bad for business —
nobody dares come out to trade anymore.
Speak up.

choices.text: How do I survive out there?
I've already killed five of them

dialogs.text:
Weapons. Armour. Things that keep people alive,
which is more than most wanderers manage out there.
If you're looking to buy, come back when I'm done.
I don't negotiate mid-swing.

Don't get hit. Ha!
In all seriousness — keep moving, and watch their feet.
Creatures telegraph their attacks with their body.
Never fight with your back to a wall.
And if you're outnumbered, run. Pride won't stop a claw.

Five of them? You're tougher than you look.
Most travellers turn tail at the first snarl.
Finish the job — wipe out every last one —
and I'll sharpen something special for you. No charge.
I respect results.

You got every last one?
I can tell when someone's bluffing.
...
You're not bluffing, are you.
Good work. Seriously.
Here — this whetstone is yours. You've earned it.
Come find me on the next level if you need more.

Oh! A living specimen — I mean, a visitor! Welcome.
I am cataloguing the creatures of this region.
Fascinating things, if you can get past the claws and the screaming.
What can I help you with?

choices.text: I've grown stronger since we met

dialogs.text:
Excellent question!
These creatures shouldn't exist this far from the dark forest.
Something is drawing them here — possibly a rift in the ley lines.
They are attracted to life energy, which is why they cluster near settlements.
Stay mobile. A stationary target is a dead one.

More questions! Wonderful, you are thorough.
My latest finding: they appear to communicate with each other.
Kill one, and the others sense it somehow.
Also — they are weakest at the joints, structurally speaking.
I would test this hypothesis myself, but I value my limbs.

Strength? It is not only a matter of muscle.
Every enemy you face teaches your body something new.
Observe the patterns, adapt, and do not repeat mistakes.
Knowledge is the sharpest weapon I know —
and I know quite a few, both literally and metaphorically.

All of them?! You wiped out the entire population?!
This is — this is extraordinary.
I have months of new research material from this alone.
You didn't happen to keep notes, did you?
No? A shame. I would have valued your field observations.

My word. You have changed since we last spoke.
Your posture. Your eyes. The way you carry yourself.
This confirms my theory entirely —
combat experience accelerates growth beyond any book.
You are living proof, traveller. Most illuminating.

Ho there! Come in, come in!
Don't mind the smell — you get used to it. I got used to it.
Although my wife says I never did and that's why she left.
Anyway! What can I do for you?

choices.text: Any tips for surviving out there?
I've been in a few fights now

dialogs.text:
Finest cuts in Galdaria!
Well. Formerly finest cuts.
The creatures killed my last two delivery men, so I'm running a bit low.
But when this mess is sorted I'll have a full stock.
Chops, roasts, sausages — you name it.
I do a lovely smoked haunch if you're interested.
Presumably not right now though. Given everything.

Nasty? Ha!
From a purely professional standpoint I'd call them interesting.
Unusual skeletal structure. Dense muscle fibre.
I am not saying I've thought about it.
I'm just saying hypothetically the cuts would be challenging.
Please don't repeat that. People misunderstand me.

Is it??
I've been a butcher for thirty years!
This is just how my brain works!
You look at a horse and think 'lovely animal'.
I look at a horse and think 'fifteen good cuts, maybe sixteen'.
Occupational hazard. I'm a perfectly nice person.

You want survival advice from a butcher?
Fair enough, I've thought about anatomy more than most.
Hit them somewhere that matters.
Every creature has a soft spot — find it early.
Also: don't fight hungry. I cannot stress this enough.
Bad decisions happen on an empty stomach.
I once saw a man charge a bear because he skipped breakfast.
He did not survive. The bear did. Tragic all around.

Every last one?!
Marvellous! This calls for a celebration!
I've got a cut of something in the back I've been saving for a special occasion.
I won't tell you what animal it's from because you'll ask questions.
Just know it smells incredible and tastes even better.
You've done this town a genuine service, friend.
Come back when I've restocked. First purchase on me.

Ha! I can tell, you know.
It's the hands. And the eyes.
People who've been in fights carry themselves differently.
More deliberate. Like they know what it costs.
You've got that look now.
Kind of unsettling on someone your size, to be honest.
I mean that as a compliment. Mostly.

Ah. A visitor.
I sensed your approach, of course.
I sense most things. It is a burden as much as a gift.
Right now I am sensing that you want something from me.
I am also sensing you haven't bathed recently, but we'll move past that.
What is it?

choices.text: Can you help me fight the creatures?
What do you know about the creatures?

dialogs.text:
Fight? Me?
I am a mage of the Seventh Conclave.
I do not fight. I illuminate. I advise. I occasionally curse people who deserve it.
Direct combat is beneath my station and also very dangerous.
Not for them. For me. I bruise easily.
But I can offer you something more valuable than a fireball.
I can offer you knowledge.

These creatures are drawn by a resonance in the ley lines.
Something below this land is singing the wrong note —
a dark frequency that calls them like moths to a flame.
The source is deeper. Further in.
Defeating the creatures here is necessary but not sufficient.
You are treating the symptom, not the disease.
But it is a start. Even mages have to start somewhere.
I started by accidentally turning my tutor into a frog. We all have our journeys.

choices.text: How do I stop it at the source?

dialogs.text:
That is an excellent question and I respect you for asking it.
Unfortunately I do not entirely know.
I know it is deep. I know it is old. I know it is angry.
Beyond that my scrying has been... cloudy.
Something is blocking my vision, which is extremely rude.
Clear this place first. Then seek the next portal.
Each step will reveal more. Probably.

Teach you magic.
In one conversation.
Right.
Magic takes twelve years of dedicated study, seventeen failed attempts at basic fire conjuring,
one crisis of faith, and at least two very bad haircuts from the stress.
I cannot give you that.
What I can give you is this: trust your instincts in the field.
The body knows things the mind is too slow to process.
That is essentially magic. Don't tell the Conclave I said that.

I know.
I felt the resonance shift the moment the last one fell.
Like a chord resolving. Rather beautiful, in a morbid way.
You have done well, traveller.
I confess I did not think you would manage it.
I am recalibrating my assessment of you upward.
That does not happen often. Enjoy the moment.

The portal will take you deeper.
The source of the disturbance awaits.
I would come with you but — 
well.
Conclaveregulations. Insurance reasons. Also a prior engagement.
But I will be watching. Scrying, technically.
You will not see me but I will be there.
That is either comforting or unsettling. I leave that to you.

Yes.
I can see it.
Your aura has changed — deeper colour, sharper edges.
In magical terms you are considerably more dangerous than when we first spoke.
In practical terms: good. You will need it.
Whatever is down there has been waiting a long time.
It will not be impressed by someone who hasn't grown.
Fortunately for you — you have.

...
...
Ah.
A small warm thing.
I have not spoken in... forty-three winters, I believe.
Possibly forty-four. Time moves differently when you are rooted.
Speak, then. I am listening.
I have nowhere else to be.

choices.text: What are those creatures out there?

dialogs.text:
A good question.
I am what this forest remembers of itself.
I was a seed when this hillside had no name.
I watched the first road get cut through that valley.
Spoiled a perfectly good meadow, that road.
But I digress.
I am old. I am large. I am largely unbothered.
Until recently.

This forest has stood for longer than your people have had words.
Every root is a memory. Every ring inside me is a year.
I have watched empires burn and flowers return in spring.
Both are, in the grand scale, equally brief.
The creatures you see out there — they did not grow here.
Something brought them.
Something wrong.

I felt them arrive before I saw them.
The soil changed. A sour note, deep underground.
They answer to something dark, beyond this wood.
They do not belong here and the forest knows it.
The birds went quiet. That is always the first sign.
When the birds go quiet, something is very wrong.
Or a cat is nearby. But in this case — very wrong.

Me?
Hm.
I am... not built for speed.
Or pursuit.
Or anything that requires moving more than two feet in a decade.
I have tried reasoning with them.
They were not interested.
You, however, appear to be both mobile and armed.
Think about it.

Good.
I would help you myself, but—
...well. You see the situation.
When you have cleared them, come back.
I will still be here.
I am always still here.
That is both my strength and my primary complaint.

...
Yes.
I can feel it.
The soil is easier now. Less... noise.
You did that.
In the time it took you, I grew perhaps half a leaf.
And yet you accomplished considerably more.
I find that humbling. And also mildly embarrassing.

The forest will recover. It always does.
Slowly. Over decades. In ways you will not live to see.
But it begins today, because of you.
That is not nothing, small warm thing.
Go further. Something still calls those creatures here.
The root of it lies beyond this wood.
I wish I could tell you more.
I am very old, but my reach is only as far as my roots.

You have changed.
I notice these things — I have been watching things change for centuries.
The way you stand. The set of your shoulders.
You carry more weight now, and not just the physical kind.
Growth, in my experience, always costs something.
But it is always worth the price.
You are doing well, small warm thing.
Better than you know.
